nodes.name: Counseling Frontend SPA
nodes.summary: React 19 + TypeScript application for askers and consultants: registration wizard, login, Matrix messaging, calls, notifications timeline, profile and legal flows. Webpack build (config/webpack) with Vite/Vitest for tests, Storybook component tests, and Playwright smoke suites; React Router v7 and MUI/M3 theming.

nodes.name: Matrix-only Real-time Communication
nodes.summary: All messaging runs over Matrix (matrix-js-sdk). matrixClientService owns the client lifecycle, chatTransportService is the send/receive facade, matrixLiveEventBridge feeds live updates into the UI. RocketChat and Jitsi are fully removed; guard tests (matrixOnlyLegacyArtifacts, matrixCredentialBoundary, legacyAppointmentProviderAbsence) fail the build if legacy tokens reappear.

nodes.name: Application Structure
nodes.summary: src is organized into api (127 HTTP client modules incl. generated OpenAPI clients), components (per-feature folders such as message, registration, notificationsCenter, erstantwort), containers, services (Matrix/call/draft services), globalState, hooks, emails, and resources/i18n with bundled catalogues for de, de@informal, en, fr, ru, ti, tr.

nodes.name: E2EE and Silent Key Backup (Tresor)
nodes.summary: Matrix E2EE is durably on. Per ADR-019 the recovery key backup is set up silently at login instead of via a setup modal: matrixKeyBackupService creates the owner-bound backup, pendingRecoveryKeyStore holds keys until confirmed, device dehydration and room-history key transfer cover new devices, and KeyBackupRecoveryPrompt only appears when recovery is actually needed.

nodes.name: Calls: Element Call Widget and LiveKit
nodes.summary: Video/audio calls use Element Call embedded in widget mode (ADR-018 'Matryoshka') over LiveKit SFU. CallManager orchestrates call state, matrixCallService/matrixGroupCallService handle Matrix signalling, useElementCallWidget hosts the embed, and a generated theme (npm run generate:call-theme) restyles Element Call to ORISO design tokens. Legacy Jitsi appointment routes survive only as redirect stubs.

nodes.name: Notifications Center / Activity Timeline (Zeitstrahl)
nodes.summary: The notifications center renders an activity timeline of event notifications with Matrix-hydrated conversation previews. Event types come from an eventDescriptors registry; previews are gated fail-closed by case-handover consent (caseHandoverPreviewGate) so consultants without consent never see message content. Backed by apiEventNotifications, active-view PATCH, and do-not-disturb settings.

nodes.name: Registration and Onboarding Wizard
nodes.summary: Multi-step registration wizard (welcome screen, topic/agency selection, zipcode, demographics, account data) with a free-navigation stepper, preselection drawers, validation modules, and auto-login into the first enquiry. The redesigned login stage adds tenant-selectable effects (lamp-map) and a security explainer; a product tour (intro.js-based ProductTourAdapter with tutorial-progress API) onboards consultants.

nodes.name: Erstantwort and Anonymous (Carimat) Chat
nodes.summary: First-response (Erstantwort) sequence for new enquiries: templated message catalogue, deadline ownership rules, save-credentials card, and an email overlay. The anonymous/pseudonym surface (Carimat) adds consent gating, bot message animations, breathing tutorial cards, animal avatars from the shared anonymous-name engine, and queue-leave dialogs.

nodes.name: Legal, DPA (AVV) and Consent Surfaces
nodes.summary: Legal/compliance UI: DPA (data processing agreement) signature flow with DpaSign and signature API, department-specific legal texts (DepartmentLegalSection, per ADR/issue #555 department selector), legal content pages and link components, terms-and-conditions, and the case-handover consent cards built on the shared ButtonGroup.

nodes.name: Media Upload and Attachments
nodes.summary: Attachments upload to the Matrix media repo (apiMatrixUpload) and send as encrypted Matrix attachment messages. mediaUploadHelpers and resolveAttachmentForSend validate type/size before send, matrixEncryptedAttachment handles encrypt/decrypt, and AttachmentCard/MessageAttachment render download cards with media checks in the timeline.

nodes.name: Case Handover
nodes.summary: Consent-based case handover between consultants: client-facing consent cards, handover notices rendered as chat system messages, i18n aligned with ADR-002, and downstream gating of timeline previews. The consent decision also controls what the receiving consultant may see.

nodes.name: Transactional E-Mail Design System
nodes.summary: src/emails is a token-based e-mail design system (atoms/molecules/organisms/templates) with content catalogues for de-du, de-sie and en dialects. vite-node build scripts render templates for Keycloak and the MailService; Storybook 'Email/*' stories preview them and tests check e-mail client compatibility and dialect consistency.

nodes.name: Consultant Statistics View
nodes.summary: Consultant statistics page in the profile area (enquiries, messages sent, appointments, CSV export via react-csv) backed by the UserService statistics endpoint; messages-sent counting is privacy-scoped server-side.

nodes.name: Asker Registration → First Chat
nodes.summary: Asker walks the registration wizard (topic/agency selection, zipcode, account data) → apiPostRegistration creates the account → autoLogin authenticates against Keycloak and registers/logs into Matrix → the enquiry is sent (encrypted payload) → the session's Matrix room opens in the messaging UI.

nodes.name: Encrypted Message Send
nodes.summary: TipTap-based composer builds the message → attachments resolve through resolveAttachmentForSend and upload via apiMatrixUpload → chatTransportService sends the (Megolm-encrypted) Matrix event → matrixLiveEventBridge delivers the echo → MessageItemComponent renders it in the timeline with three-state delivery status; failures surface as FailedSendTimelineEntry, drafts persist via draftStore.

nodes.name: Silent Key Backup Setup
nodes.summary: After login the Matrix crypto stack initialises → matrixKeyBackupService silently creates or connects the key backup (owner-bound setup lock, no user dialog per ADR-019) → the recovery key is parked in pendingRecoveryKeyStore → the user is only prompted (KeyBackupRecoveryPrompt) if history cannot be decrypted on a fresh device.

nodes.name: Call Invite → Element Call Join
nodes.summary: A call invite arrives over Matrix → IncomingVideoCall surfaces it → CallManager coordinates accept/decline and room state → the Element Call widget (useElementCallWidget, matrix-widget-api) is embedded with the generated ORISO theme → media flows E2EE via LiveKit; group calls go through matrixGroupCallService.

nodes.name: Admin Dashboard SPA
nodes.summary: React 19 + TypeScript single-page admin application built with Vite. UI is a hybrid of Ant Design 5 (with the React-19 patch) and MUI 9, both themed to the muted M3 scheme. Pages are lazy-loaded via lazyPages, runtime configuration is generated into env.js at container start, and OpenTelemetry web-vitals metrics are emitted from the browser.

nodes.name: Management Domains (Pages)
nodes.summary: The admin UI is organized by management domains under src/pages: Agency (list/edit with FieldGrid master data), Links (invites), TenantSettings (theme/global settings tabs), Tenants, Topics, users (accounts/agency-admins/tenant-admins/platform-admins tables), Statistic, Logs (case-handover, inactive-accounts, supervisor), Profile, Login, PasswordReset, and the public TenantOnboarding wizard. Which settings tabs render is derived per role/permission in settingsTabs.

nodes.name: API Layer
nodes.summary: src/api holds per-domain HTTP client modules (tenant, agency, admins, counselor, user, settings, statistic, invitelinks, accountInvites, tenantOnboarding, passwordReset, idAllocation, tutorial) built on a shared fetchData wrapper. Endpoint URLs are centralized in appConfig.ts and point at UserService, TenantService, AgencyService and ConsultingTypeService; data fetching/caching in the UI goes through TanStack Query v5 hooks under src/hooks.

nodes.name: M3 Design System and AntD→MUI Migration
nodes.summary: A muted Material 3 token scheme drives both UI libraries: antdM3Theme maps M3 tokens into the AntD ConfigProvider while orisoMuiTheme themes MUI 9. Custom M3 components (M3Button, M3Switch, M3FabMenu, M3NumberField, MuiFormField and friends) progressively replace AntD widgets; the migration is deliberate and incremental — AntD is still imported in roughly 179 files versus around 42 MUI files — with Form.Item kept as the form scaffolding during conversion. The mui9/antd inventory doc tracks remaining surfaces.

nodes.name: Mobile Navigation (Thumb-Reachable Redesign)
nodes.summary: New mobile navigation shell: a floating action button menu (M3FabMenu) opens the AdminMobileNav which mirrors the desktop sidebar, with per-page secondary rows, section pills and a MobileNavProvider context. Replaces the folded sidebar on small viewports; a provider re-render loop that froze the whole admin panel after one navigation was fixed in #707.

nodes.name: Statistics Dashboard
nodes.summary: Card-based statistics dashboard fed by the UserService useradmin statistics endpoints: a dashboard endpoint for platform metrics and a tutorial-statistics endpoint for onboarding-tour completion. StatisticCard renders animated values with per-metric menus and calm empty-state hints ('not yet collected') instead of fake zeros; user card preferences persist via statisticPreferences.

nodes.name: Legal Texts and DPA (AVV) Module
nodes.summary: Legal settings manage imprint, privacy and DPA content per tenant, department and agency with a TipTap-based M3 rich-text editor (FormPluginEditor). Editors open on the legal source language (pinned even when languages load late), warn on publish when the source language was left untouched, and can machine-translate on publish. The DPA side adds versioned agreements, signature tracking, DPA invite emails, and a DpaBlockerGate that locks the admin UI until the organisation DPA is signed.

nodes.name: Tenant-Admin Onboarding Wizard
nodes.summary: Public (unauthenticated) onboarding flow at /admin/tenant-onboarding/{rawToken}: an emailed account-invite link leads through account creation, organisation DPA acceptance and a mandatory-or-deferrable 2FA setup step before landing in the admin panel. Token handling and step state live in useTenantAdminOnboardingFlow; the backend counterpart is the UserService AccountInviteService.

nodes.name: Links and Invite Composer
nodes.summary: The Links page unifies invitation management: an InviteComposer for counsellor and tenant-admin invites (with derived department routing), account-invite tables with bulk actions, CSV bulk import, an email-template dialog with live EmailTemplatePreview, and an external-inbounds tab. Invites are sent through UserService invitelinks / account-invites / invite-email-templates endpoints.

nodes.name: Permissions Settings and Role Model
nodes.summary: Function-access settings render permission cards per audience (super-admin, tenant, agency, asker) with toggles constrained by granular access rules and an enforce-mode footer switch. Client-side gating maps Keycloak roles to PermissionAction/Resource pairs via userRolesToPermissions and the useUserPermission hook, which also decides which settings tabs and nav entries are visible.

nodes.name: Authentication, Password Reset and 2FA
nodes.summary: Keycloak-backed login with token/session helpers under src/api/auth and route protection via ProtectedRoute. A self-service password-reset flow (request + confirm pages) and per-user two-factor setup (authenticator app or email OTP) are first-class: TwoFactorSetup components serve both the profile page and the onboarding wizard, with a deferral hook for postponable setup.

nodes.name: Login → Manage Platform Entities
nodes.summary: Admin signs in (Login page, Keycloak-backed; 2FA where enabled) → ProtectedRoute admits the role → a lazy-loaded management page renders → data loads through TanStack Query hooks over the src/api clients → edits are written back to the owning backend service (UserService, TenantService, AgencyService, ConsultingTypeService).

nodes.name: Invite Email → Tenant-Admin Onboarding
nodes.summary: Admin composes an account invite (Links page) → UserService emails a link containing a raw token → invitee opens /admin/tenant-onboarding/{token} → creates the account → accepts the organisation DPA → completes (or defers) 2FA setup → lands in the admin panel; until the DPA is signed the DpaBlockerGate keeps the rest of the UI locked.

nodes.name: Legal Text Edit → Publish
nodes.summary: Editor opens a legal document (imprint/privacy/DPA) for a tenant, department or agency → the TipTap editor pins the legal source language → on publish, a warning fires if only translations changed while the source language stayed untouched, and translate-on-publish can regenerate translations → published text is served to the app layer and gates registration/consent there.

nodes.name: Statistics Dashboard Load
nodes.summary: Statistic page mounts → useStatisticDashboardData queries the UserService useradmin statistics/dashboard endpoint (tutorial stats separately) → responses map into card view-models → StatisticCard animates values, or renders the muted empty-state hint when a metric is not collected yet → card layout preferences persist per user.

nodes.name: Consultation Session Lifecycle
nodes.summary: UserService owns the consultation lifecycle: registration of new users/askers, handling and creation of enquiries, creation of sessions with their encrypted Matrix rooms, and assignment of consultants with the matching room memberships. The former monolithic UserController is split into focused delegates (registration, sessions, chats, consultants, account, support, 2FA).

nodes.name: Consultation Modes
nodes.summary: Four kinds of consultations are handled: single/direct 1:1 counseling, team counseling, group chat counseling, and anonymous counseling (no registration required). Anonymous enquiries enforce server-side data-privacy confirmation on the assign path.

nodes.name: Matrix-only Messaging
nodes.summary: Messaging is Matrix-only: the Rocket.Chat adapter, its API contracts, and the rocketChat* database columns were removed (migrations 0073-0075), with contract tests asserting the adapter stays gone. MatrixMessageController sends/fetches session messages, MatrixSyncController keeps read models in sync, MatrixSynapseService plus room/user clients manage Synapse accounts and rooms, and RedisMessageMirrorService mirrors messages for fast session-list previews.

nodes.name: Session Media Upload & Download Proxy
nodes.summary: File sharing in counselling sessions goes through UserService as a proxy to the Matrix media repository: POST /matrix/sessions/{sessionId}/upload uploads the file, posts the matching m.room.message file event, and GET /matrix/media/download/{serverName}/{mediaId} proxies authenticated downloads. Content scanning (ADR-014/015 fail-closed scanner) is a platform-level concern and not yet enforced inside this repo.

nodes.name: User & Consultant Administration
nodes.summary: Admin-facing account management: UserAdminController with ConsultantAdminFacade and AskerUserAdminFacade cover consultant/asker administration, agency assignment, and account state; consultant lifecycle is hardened (status transitions, pre-deletion validation) and counsellors can also be provisioned from accepted account invites.

nodes.name: Identity Ports & Second Factor (2FA/OTP)
nodes.summary: Keycloak access is split behind narrow hexagonal Identity* ports (IdentityLogin, IdentitySecondFactor, IdentityProfileUpdater, IdentityEmailAddressUpdater, ...) implemented by KeycloakService, so callers depend on capabilities instead of the Keycloak client. Second-factor auth (email OTP and app TOTP via the Keycloak extension) runs through IdentitySecondFactor with per-role identity.otp-allowed-* flags; account invites can pre-provision a pending TOTP secret so 2FA is active on first login.

nodes.name: Case Handover
nodes.summary: CaseHandoverController implements transferring cases between consultants/agencies: persisted CaseHandoverRequest entities governed by per-tenant CaseHandoverReasonPolicy records, audit logging via CaseHandoverLogsService, and notification templates (migration 0069) for the parties involved.

nodes.name: Invite Links, Account Invites & Provisioning
nodes.summary: Invitation-based onboarding: agency invite links plus account invites with reservation tokens, tracked invite-email templates and delivery status, and a compensating ProvisioningWorkflow that creates the Keycloak, Matrix, and database resources for a counsellor when an invite is accepted (rolling back partial resources on failure). DpaForwardEmailController lets a candidate forward the data-processing agreement before accepting.

nodes.name: Live Availability & Presence
nodes.summary: ConsultantLiveAvailabilityController and TopicConsultantAvailabilityController expose consultant availability backed by a Redis-based ConsultantActivityRegistry and Matrix presence. The LiveService proxy is retired: DeprecatedLiveProxyController remains only as a compatibility shim and the liveservice/messageservice outbound contracts were deleted.

nodes.name: Event Notification Center (Timeline Backend)
nodes.summary: Persisted EventNotification records back the frontend notification center/timeline: message events arrive on a dual path (REST message-events endpoint and the Matrix timeline listener) and are deduplicated via a bounded dedup key and correlated by Matrix event id, ordered with millisecond precision (migrations 0063/0080). Active-conversation-view heartbeats with TTL expiry suppress notifications for rooms the user is looking at; PrivacyEnvelope, per-room NotificationRoomLevel, and Do-Not-Disturb windows control content and delivery.

nodes.name: Erstantwort (First Response, ADR-018)
nodes.summary: When an enquiry lands on the Matrix path, the service produces a FIRST_RESPONSE and posts exactly one persisted [SYSTEM_NOTIFICATION] event that carries the whole Erstantwort: ErstantwortPayloadBuilder resolves each Baustein against the session's configuration and freezes the resulting wording into the payload so later template edits cannot retroactively change what an advice seeker was told. It deliberately stores no completion state and creates no Matrix bot account (Carimat is a rendering identity only).

nodes.name: Statistics & Audit Logs
nodes.summary: Three statistics surfaces: AdminStatisticsController feeds the admin dashboard, ConsultantStatisticsController exposes consultant metrics including messages-sent counted from Matrix events into ConsultantMessageStat rows keyed by an HMAC-hashed consultant identity (statistics.message-count.hmac-secret) with small-cell suppression, and UserStatisticsController serves session statistics. Domain statistics events (registration, assignment, video calls, archive/delete) are emitted to the statistics exchange; InactiveAccountAuditLogsController and SupervisorLogsController provide audit trails.

nodes.name: MatrixRTC Call Policy
nodes.summary: Authorization backend for MatrixRTC/Element Call: MatrixRtcCallPolicyController verifies a signed policy token, resolves the policy in the technical tenant context, and answers whether media may flow for a room, with typed denial reasons and HMAC-keyed correlation ids so raw Matrix identifiers never appear in denial logs.

nodes.name: Group Chats & Team Discussions
nodes.summary: Group chat counseling on Matrix rooms, extended with self-help group series (recurring chats, occurrence exceptions, per-series participant roles, author content; migrations 0060-0064), membership managed by GroupChatMembershipService, plus reminder and lifecycle notifications. Internal team chats open immediately on creation instead of parking in the waiting area, and TeamDiscussion side-rooms let a department discuss an enquiry before acceptance.

nodes.name: Support Rooms & Live Handshake
nodes.summary: HandshakeController implements audited, purpose-bound handshake sessions (HandshakeSession + HandshakeAuditEvent, migration 0078) used to grant scoped access, e.g. for support; SupportRoomController manages dedicated support rooms (migration 0079, with a schema self-repair changeset 0081) where platform support can assist users without entering counselling rooms.

nodes.name: Scheduled Workflows & Task Claim Leases
nodes.summary: Cron-driven workflows (account deletion, registered-only deletion, anonymous deactivation/deletion, enquiry notifications, inactive-account notifications) now acquire a database lease via ScheduledTaskClaim (migration 0082) before running, so only one replica executes each task and reruns are safe. Deletion supports a read-only window and pause period before data is removed.

nodes.name: Appointments (Legacy Remnant)
nodes.summary: The appointment subsystem (AppointmentController, appointmentservice.yaml, Appointment entity, delete-job cron) is a remnant of the upstream Calcom-style booking integration; feature.appointment.enabled defaults to false and the code has only been touched by cross-cutting refactors since July. ADR-020 scheduled calls are not implemented here.

nodes.name: Enquiry → Session → Consultant Assignment
nodes.summary: An asker registers → creates an enquiry (Matrix-only; encrypted enquiries are finalized as encrypted Matrix events and plaintext bodies are rejected when encryption is expected) → a session with its Matrix room is created; for department sessions the consultants join the holding room before the asker → a consultant (or team) is assigned and room memberships are updated.

nodes.name: Matrix Message Roundtrip
nodes.summary: Client sends via MatrixMessageController → the message lands in the session's Matrix room via Synapse → RedisMessageMirrorService mirrors it for session-list previews and MatrixSyncController keeps read models in sync; file attachments take the upload proxy through MatrixMediaClient.

nodes.name: Erstantwort First Response (ADR-018)
nodes.summary: An enquiry arrives on the Matrix path → the service emits FIRST_RESPONSE and posts one persisted [SYSTEM_NOTIFICATION] event whose payload freezes the resolved Erstantwort Bausteine (greeting, actions, legal texts) for this session → the frontend renders it via the Carimat identity; completion of action items is always read live, never stored in the event.

nodes.name: Notification Center Event Flow
nodes.summary: A message or session event arrives via REST (/users/event-notifications/message-events) or the Matrix timeline listener → EventNotificationDeduplicationWriter collapses the dual paths with a bounded dedup key and the Matrix event id → the EventNotification is persisted with millisecond ordering and content metadata → clients poll the feed; fresh active-view heartbeats suppress notifications for the room currently on screen, and stale views expire by TTL.

nodes.name: Counsellor Invite → Provisioning
nodes.summary: An admin creates an account invite (reservation token, optional pending TOTP secret) → the invite email is rendered from tracked templates and its delivery status recorded → on acceptance the ProvisioningWorkflow creates the Keycloak account, Matrix user, and consultant records step by step, compensating already-created resources if a later step fails.

nodes.name: Case Handover Flow
nodes.summary: A consultant requests a case handover citing a tenant-configured reason policy → the CaseHandoverRequest is persisted and the receiving side is notified via handover notification templates → on acceptance the session, Matrix room memberships, and responsibilities transfer, with the trail recorded by CaseHandoverLogsService.

nodes.name: Counseling Agency Registry
nodes.summary: Spring Boot service managing counseling agencies (Beratungsstellen) for the platform: agency master data, addresses, settings, and public agency lookup used during asker registration. Agencies belong to a Träger (tenant) and carry per-agency feature settings served to the counselling app.

nodes.name: Agency Administration
nodes.summary: AgencyAdminController plus AgencyAdminService cover the admin-facing lifecycle: creating, updating, and configuring agencies, topic assignment, admin controls, postcode ranges, and the ADR-014 legal-text library endpoints. The admin OpenAPI contract (agencyadminservice.yaml) grew substantially in July/August 2026 with agency-ID allocation, legal-text CRUD, and department legal endpoints.

nodes.name: Agency Search & Matching
nodes.summary: Public agency search resolves the right agency for an asker (postcode/topic-based matching) before registration completes. Since #194/#196 the topic aggregation only reports topics a help-seeker can actually reach (reachability filter in AgencyRepository), so offline/hidden agencies no longer leak topics into registration.

nodes.name: Department Legal Texts (ADR-003 / ADR-014)
nodes.summary: A department (Fachbereich = agency x topic, AgencyTopic entity) carries a data privacy policy (DPP) and imprint. ADR-014 adds a tenant-owned reusable LegalText library: several departments may share one text per kind, or fall back to their inline content. Content is a JSON language-to-HTML map, OWASP-sanitised by LegalContentSanitizer. Publishing a department-specific edit breaks the shared link (#193); agencies also got agency-level legal texts the inheritance chain assumed (#222, changeset 0027). Only PUBLISHED texts are served to end users via the unauthenticated read side.

nodes.name: Agency ID Allocation (TEN-INV-U2)
nodes.summary: Collision-free, DB-arbitrated allocation of agency IDs for the tenant-invite flow (parent ORISO-Admin#569). IDs are FREE, RESERVED (open invite holds a row in agency_id_reservation, PK = the ID) or ASSIGNED (agency row, never re-issued, soft-deleted included). Assignment checks run as native SQL so a tenant-scoped admin's Hibernate tenant filter can never hide another Träger's agency and report a taken ID as free. Concurrency safety comes from the primary key and write-then-read transactions, not app-level checks.

nodes.name: Effective Permission Settings (ADR-013 P4)
nodes.summary: AgencyEffectivePermissionSettingsApplier applies upper-role permission constraints (AgencyAdminControls) to the public feature flags served to the counselling app: allowed=false forces a feature off, enforced=true forces it on, otherwise the agency's own setting stands (#297). Mirrors TenantService's applier at agency level; the server is the single source of truth and the raw controls are never attached to the public agency response. Agency settings also mirror the media flag families (upload / inline display / AI scan, per chat type) from the media epic; the old attachment flag is retired.

nodes.name: Multitenancy & Cross-Träger Isolation
nodes.summary: Tenant resolution chain (access token, custom header, subdomain, technical user) feeds TenantContext; TenantAspect enables the Hibernate tenant filter on tenant-aware repositories so one Träger's admins cannot see another's agencies. Agency admins without a domain user claim are tolerated since #143. Deliberate escape hatches (tenant-unaware repository, native-SQL checks in ID allocation) exist where global uniqueness matters.

nodes.name: Matrix Agency Provisioning
nodes.summary: Each agency gets a Matrix bot/user provisioned via the Synapse admin API (MatrixProvisioningService). Since AS-C01 the per-agency Matrix passwords are encrypted at rest (AgencyMatrixPasswordCipher, AES) and the internal credentials endpoint is protected. Rocket.Chat configuration and its residual environment contract were fully removed (#191); the service is Matrix-only and CI attests Matrix-only images.

nodes.name: Agency Deletion & Purge Workflow
nodes.summary: Cron-driven delete workflow: agencies flagged deleted are purged in batch, but since #202 each agency purges inside its own REQUIRES_NEW transaction (AgencyPurgeTransaction) so one failure no longer takes the whole batch down and gets a per-agency log line. Departments (agency_topic) are removed via JPA cascade/orphanRemoval, an explicit redundant delete was dropped (#220); postcode ranges need the explicit delete.

nodes.name: Admin Agency List Sorting
nodes.summary: GET /agencyadmin/agencies supports whitelist-based sorting via the generated Sort.FieldEnum; SortParameterBindingConfig binds the admin frontend's upper-cased separator-free field names (POSTCODE, CREATEDATE) leniently onto the underscore enum constants instead of rejecting them with HTTP 400 (Admin#308 / AS#128 package). The enum acts as the sort-field whitelist.

nodes.name: Agency Lookup During Registration
nodes.summary: Asker enters registration context -> public agency search (AgencyController) matches by postcode/consulting type/topic, reporting only reachable topics -> effective permission settings are applied server-side to the returned feature flags -> selected agency determines the consulting setup downstream.

nodes.name: Legal Text Authoring to Public Read
nodes.summary: Tenant admin authors a reusable LegalText (or inline department text) -> LegalContentSanitizer cleans multilingual HTML -> text is assigned to departments; publishing a department-specific edit breaks the shared link -> once PUBLISHED, end users read it unauthenticated via /agencies/{agencyId}/topics/{topicId}/legal (DepartmentLegalService); drafts never reach clients.

nodes.name: Agency ID Reservation and Creation
nodes.summary: Admin invite flow checks /agencyadmin/agencyids/{id}/availability or asks for next-free -> reservation row inserted (PK arbitration, write-then-read) -> agency creation guards against open reservations inside its insert transaction -> IDs are never re-issued, even for soft-deleted agencies.

nodes.name: Scheduled Agency Purge
nodes.summary: agency.deleteworkflow.cron triggers DeleteAgencyService -> each deleted-flagged agency is purged in its own REQUIRES_NEW transaction (AgencyPurgeTransaction) -> postcode ranges deleted explicitly, departments cascade via JPA -> failures are isolated and logged per agency.

nodes.name: Consulting Type Configurations
nodes.summary: Spring Boot 4 (Java 21) service managing consulting type configurations: the per-consulting-type settings stored in MongoDB that drive registration, session behavior, and feature toggles across the platform. Public read endpoints (basic/extended/full, by slug, by tenant) plus an admin API for create/update.

nodes.name: Topics & Topic Groups
nodes.summary: TopicController, TopicAdminController, and TopicGroupsController with TopicServiceFacade manage counseling topics and their grouping — the taxonomy agencies and consultants are matched against. Topics are multilingual (i18n-aware name/description), carry fallback agency/URL and welcome-message settings, and live in MariaDB via Liquibase-managed schema. The published OpenAPI contract was corrected in July 2026 (issue #96): welcomeMessage/fallbackUrl are plain strings, ids are integer/int64.

nodes.name: Application Settings & Global SMTP
nodes.summary: ApplicationSettingsController and ApplicationSettingsServiceFacade expose platform-wide application settings (Mongo-backed) consumed by other services and the frontends. Since mid-2026 they also carry the global SMTP configuration: passwords are encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM (SmtpPasswordEncryptionService) only when settings.smtp.password.encryption.secret is configured — without that secret the service silently falls back to storing them plaintext at rest and credentials are no longer leaked through the public /settings endpoint.

nodes.name: DPA (AVV) Signing Email Dispatch
nodes.summary: New since July 2026 (TEN-INV-U5): POST /settingsadmin/dpa-signing-emails sends the one-time DPA/AVV signing link to a tenant contact using the global SMTP settings. DpaSigningEmailService pins the sign link to the configured app origin and the /dpa-sign/ path, builds a German HTML mail, and returns a strict success-or-error receipt; JakartaDpaMailTransport enforces STARTTLS (mail.smtp.starttls.required) and server-identity verification, classifying unparseable recipients as 400 and SMTP failures as 502 (SmtpSendException). Known drift: this endpoint is deliberately absent from every OpenAPI spec, so contract gates do not cover it.

nodes.name: Tenant Resolution & Isolation
nodes.summary: Multitenancy support: HttpTenantFilter and TenantResolver establish the tenant per request, TenantContext holds it thread-locally, and TenantAspect plus tenant-aware repositories scope data access. Hardened July 2026 (#43): when a subdomain is present it is authoritative — a tenantId header that contradicts the subdomain-derived tenant is rejected with AccessDenied instead of being trusted; the header fallback remains only for genuine internal service-to-service calls.

nodes.name: OpenAPI Provider/Consumer Contract Gate
nodes.summary: New since July 2026 (#96/#51): CI publishes the provider OpenAPI bundles and runs an oasdiff breaking-change gate against the previous contracts, with a reviewed one-time allowlist for accepted corrections (contracts/topic-format-correction-96.md). Python meta-tests under tests/ci and tests/contracts assert that the gate and the required integration-test suite actually execute in CI rather than silently passing.

nodes.name: Observability: OTLP to SigNoz
nodes.summary: OBS-P2/OBS-P5 (July 2026): traces and metrics ship via OTLP to the SigNoz gateway collector (sampling pinned to 100% on Pre-Dev), logs are JSON-structured via logback-spring.xml, and CorrelationIdFilter propagates X-Correlation-ID into the SLF4J MDC (key CID) with the same naming as UserService so requests correlate across services. The Sentry SDK was removed once SigNoz reached parity.

nodes.name: Liquibase Schema Management (re-enabled)
nodes.summary: Liquibase was re-enabled in July 2026 with a single master changelog (consultingtypeservice-master.xml) for all environments, replacing the per-environment masters; contexts select environment-specific changesets and are overridable via SPRING_LIQUIBASE_CONTEXTS (Pre-Dev override, #112). Spring Boot 4 dropped Liquibase from the default classpath, so spring-boot-starter-liquibase is an explicit dependency and guard tests fail the build if the auto-configuration silently disappears again.

nodes.name: Spring Boot 4 / Java 21 Migration Fixes
nodes.summary: The service runs on Spring Boot 4.0.1 with Java 21. SB4-specific fixes landed June/July 2026: the Mongo URI property was renamed to spring.mongodb.uri (the old spring.data.mongodb.uri key is no longer bound — the earlier live breakage is fixed at this commit), TrailingSlashFilter restores the trailing-slash request matching SB4 removed, and Liquibase needs its explicit starter (see the migrations concept).

nodes.name: Topic Administration
nodes.summary: Admin creates or updates topics/topic groups (TopicAdminController) → TopicValidationService and TopicServiceFacade validate and persist → topics become available for agency/consultant matching and registration.

nodes.name: DPA Signing Email Dispatch
nodes.summary: Caller with AUTHORIZATION_PATCH_APPLICATION_SETTINGS (UserService DPA/AVV flow) POSTs recipient, tenant name, sign link, and expiry → DpaSigningEmailService validates the link against the configured app origin and /dpa-sign/ path → loads global SMTP settings and decrypts the password → JakartaDpaMailTransport sends with mandatory STARTTLS and server-identity check → 200 with a SENT receipt only after the SMTP server accepted the message; 502 on transport failure, 400 on invalid recipient.

nodes.name: Tenant Request Resolution
nodes.summary: Incoming request → HttpTenantFilter triggers resolution → TenantResolver derives the tenant from the request subdomain (authoritative) and rejects a contradicting tenantId header; without a subdomain the header is used for internal calls → TenantContext carries the tenant for the request → tenant-aware repositories and the Hibernate interceptor scope all reads/writes.

nodes.name: Tenant Registry
nodes.summary: TenantService is the ORISO tenant registry: it stores tenant identity, subdomain, licensing limits, theming, feature settings, multilingual legal content, and content activation dates. Since mid-2026 it also owns the tenant-ID allocation ledger, the DPA (Auftragsverarbeitungsvertrag) signature/status subsystem, tenant-owned media blobs, and machine translation of legal texts. Restricted public tenant metadata is served to callers without a full authenticated tenant context.

nodes.name: OpenAPI Contract & Generated Interfaces
nodes.summary: api/tenantservice.yaml defines the public REST contract. TenantController implements the generated API interfaces and applies endpoint authorization. Endpoint groups: /tenantadmin (administration, search, controls), /tenantadmin/tenant-ids/* (ID allocation and reservations), /tenantadmin/{id}/dpa/* (DPA status, versions, signing, invite, gate), /tenantadmin/translation/* and /tenant/translate/* (machine translation), /tenantadmin/media plus /media/{mediaId} (tenant media), and restricted public reads including the batch lookup /tenant/public/ids. A CI contract gate (tests/contracts) verifies provider-consumer compatibility against peer services.

nodes.name: Keycloak JWT Authorization
nodes.summary: WebSecurityConfig, JwtAuthConverter, and AuthorisationService map Keycloak-issued JWTs to local authorities; TenantFacadeAuthorisationService enforces facade-level authorization rules. The DPA facade re-uses assertUserIsAuthorizedToAccessTenant as the IDOR guard in front of the raw-tenant-id DPA services.

nodes.name: Tenant Context Resolution
nodes.summary: TenantResolverService resolves the effective tenant context from the access token, cookies, or subdomain — the mechanism behind multi-tenant request routing. SingleDomainTenantOverrideService covers the single-domain operation mode.

nodes.name: Downstream Service Synchronization
nodes.summary: ConsultingTypeService, ApplicationSettingsService, and UserAdminService call other ORISO services through generated OpenAPI clients so tenant changes propagate (consulting types, application settings, admin users).

nodes.name: MariaDB Persistence & Liquibase
nodes.summary: TenantService, TenantRepository, and the tenant entities own MariaDB persistence for tenant records, admin controls, DPA versions/signatures, tenant media blobs, and the tenant-ID reservation ledger. Liquibase is wired to a single default changelog (tenantservice-master.xml, changesets 0001-0027) with spring.liquibase.enabled defaulting to false via SPRING_LIQUIBASE_ENABLED and disabled in the testing profile; a schema-drift IT compares the changelog against the JPA model.

nodes.name: Templates & Legal Content Translations
nodes.summary: TemplateService and TranslationService manage templated, multilingual content (e.g. legal texts) with FreeMarker configuration; ConfigurationFileLoader and ConfigurationValidator load and validate template descriptions. TranslationFacade adds LLM-backed machine translation of legal texts and group-chat author content via pluggable OpenAI-compatible providers (OpenRouter, Mistral); per-tenant provider API keys live in the tenant admin controls settings and are masked by ApiKeyMasker in every response and log line.

nodes.name: DPA (AVV) Signature & Status Module
nodes.summary: The data processing agreement (Auftragsverarbeitungsvertrag) module records tenant confirmations of the DPA and derives the authoritative signed/unsigned gate. GoverningDpaResolver is the single source of truth for which versioned document governs a tenant (its own published DPA if it authored one, otherwise the operator document held by app.dpa.operator-tenant-id, per #569): reading, in-app signing, and forward-for-signature all resolve through it so status and signable document never diverge. Two signing channels count: token-based public confirmation (hashed, single-use, expiring DpaSignToken consumed atomically) and audit-proof in-app signing by authenticated tenant admins (append-only tenant_dpa_admin_signature). DENIED confirmations are auto-purged after a configurable retention window (default 365 days).

nodes.name: Tenant-ID Allocation Ledger
nodes.summary: Authoritative allocation of tenant IDs (TEN-INV-U1): an ID is FREE, RESERVED (held by an open invite) or ASSIGNED (consumed by a real tenant). Every reservation and tenant creation writes a row into the tenant_id_reservation ledger inside the allocating transaction, so the primary key — not an application-level check — guarantees an ID is handed out exactly once. AUTO mode assigns the smallest free ID and retries lost races in a fresh transaction; ID 0 is the technical tenant and never assignable. Exposed under /tenantadmin/tenant-ids/* (availability, next-free, reservations).

nodes.name: Tenant Media Storage
nodes.summary: TenantMediaService stores and serves tenant-owned editor images as MariaDB blobs (max 2 MB). Content type is derived from magic bytes only — client-supplied file name and content type are untrusted; SVG is deliberately unsupported (script content) and anything unrecognised is rejected fail-closed. Upload goes through /tenantadmin/media, public serving through /media/{mediaId}.

nodes.name: Platform Permission Controls & Effective Settings
nodes.summary: TenantAdminControls hold platform-level allowed/enforced permission toggles per tenant. EffectivePermissionSettingsApplier applies them server-side to the public feature flags served to the counselling app (allowed=false forces a feature off, enforced=true forces it on), so the Frontend needs no awareness of the controls, which are stripped from the restricted DTO (ADR-013 P4). The tenant settings model is the platform-wide definition point for feature flags, including the media flag families (upload / inline display / AI scan per chat type), featureTeamDiscussionEnabled, registration e-mail config (emailVisible/emailRequired), and the asker permission keys featureDisplayNameEditable and featureAskerEmailEnabled (#602).

nodes.name: Theming & Branding Asset Safety
nodes.summary: Tenant theming persists colors (including the light accent and signal colour added via changeset 0027) plus logo, favicon, and association logo. Branding assets are validated as URLs or as an allowlist of image data URLs (png/jpeg/ico; SVG deliberately absent) via InputSanitizer#sanitizeAssetUrl instead of being HTML-sanitized — the earlier HTML sanitization corrupted asset URLs and made tenant logos disappear from public surfaces. Legal-content HTML is sanitized with a restricted anchor-id slug charset for the legal anchor navigation.

nodes.name: Observability (OTLP, JSON Logs, Correlation IDs)
nodes.summary: The service ships OTLP tracing and metrics through Spring Boot 4 micrometer-tracing/OpenTelemetry auto-configuration, JSON structured logging, a correlation-id filter, and catch-all exception logging in ExceptionHandlerAdvice. The Sentry SDK was removed (OBS-P5); a tracing smoke IT guards the autoconfiguration wiring.

nodes.name: Tenant Create/Update/Delete/Search
nodes.summary: TenantController receives the request (generated API interface + endpoint authorization) → TenantServiceFacade orchestrates (change detection, dependent settings override, downstream sync) → TenantService/TenantRepository persist to MariaDB → converters map between DTOs and entities. Creation allocates the tenant ID through the reservation ledger (AUTO or invite-reserved), preserves DPA fields on update, and search supports sorting by NAME, SUBDOMAIN and BERATERCOUNT.

nodes.name: Restricted Public Tenant Metadata
nodes.summary: Unauthenticated or partially-authenticated callers fetch restricted public tenant metadata (branding, subdomain lookup, batch lookup via /tenant/public/ids) before a full tenant context exists — resolved via TenantResolverService and served through restricted read endpoints. EffectivePermissionSettingsApplier merges platform permission controls into the served feature flags, and the controls themselves are stripped from the restricted DTO.

nodes.name: DPA Signing & Gate
nodes.summary: TenantDpaFacade guards every admin-facing DPA call with tenant authorization (IDOR guard) → GoverningDpaResolver picks the governing document/version (own published DPA or operator DPA) → TenantDpaStatusService derives the authoritative status from the version in force, the append-only admin signature audit trail, and legacy token signatures. Signing happens either in-app (authenticated tenant admin, audit fields recorded) or via a forwarded public link: a hashed single-use expiring token whose preview and confirmation (/tenant/public/dpa/confirm/{token}) are consumed atomically, with concurrent double-submits absorbed. The derived gate blocks tenants whose governing DPA is unsigned; version history recovers the gate when a tenant's own version list is empty.

nodes.name: Tenant Media Upload & Public Serve
nodes.summary: An admin uploads an editor image via /tenantadmin/media → TenantMediaService enforces the 2 MB limit, detects the content type from magic bytes (rejecting SVG and anything unrecognised), and stores the blob with a UUID in MariaDB → the image is served publicly by /media/{mediaId} with the detected content type, so tenant legal/branding content can reference stable media URLs.

nodes.name: Legal Text Machine Translation
nodes.summary: A tenant admin stores provider API keys via /tenantadmin/translation/keys (masked in responses by ApiKeyMasker) → /tenantadmin/translate sends legal-text HTML to the configured OpenAI-compatible provider (OpenRouter or Mistral) through TranslationFacade → translated multilingual content is stored alongside translation metadata (documented in documentation/translation-meta.md). /tenant/translate/group-chat-author-content covers on-demand translation of group-chat author content.

nodes.name: ORISO-Database
nodes.summary: Repository ORISO-Database — 89 nodes, 87 edges, built from c9630a93, 9 domain concepts/flows.

nodes.name: Archived Repository (Analysis-Only)
nodes.summary: ORISO-Database is ARCHIVED upstream and frozen at June 2026. It was the interim central schema store while services ran with Liquibase disabled; canonical schema management has since moved back to per-service Liquibase changelogs in each service repository, with deployment/infra owned by ORISO-Helm. Treat everything here as a historical snapshot for analysis and forensics, not as a deployment source.

nodes.name: Central Schema Authority (historical model)
nodes.summary: The repository's original operating model: all backend services (TenantService, UserService, AgencyService, ConsultingTypeService) ran with Liquibase DISABLED and schemas were version-controlled and applied from here. This model is retired — the repo is archived and per-service Liquibase is being re-enabled service by service (environments still running SPRING_LIQUIBASE_ENABLED=false rely on Helm-shipped SQL baselines instead of service changelogs) — but the schema.sql exports remain useful as a point-in-time reference of the June 2026 database state (DATABASECHANGELOG tables are still present in every dump).

nodes.name: MariaDB Schemas (7 databases, June 2026 snapshot)
nodes.summary: Per-service mysqldump exports for agencyservice, consultingtypeservice, tenantservice, userservice, videoservice, uploadservice, and the empty shared caritas database. The userservice snapshot (27 tables) already includes the case handover subsystem (case_handover_request, case_handover_reason_policy), event_notification, appointment, draft_message, and identity_tombstone; the tenantservice snapshot includes the address/description columns added in June 2026.

nodes.name: Matrix Migration Dual-Column Snapshot
nodes.summary: The userservice schema is frozen mid-migration: user, consultant, session, and chat tables carry BOTH legacy RocketChat columns (rc_user_id, rc_group_id) AND Matrix columns (matrix_user_id, matrix_room_id, matrix_password). The live platform has since completed the Matrix-only migration; this dump documents the transitional shape only. Matrix Synapse's own PostgreSQL schema was never captured (see postgresql/matrix/STATUS.md).

nodes.name: Polyglot Stores (MongoDB, PostgreSQL, RabbitMQ, Redis)
nodes.summary: Beyond MariaDB: MongoDB BSON dumps of consulting types and application settings (duplicated under consulting_types/ and consultingtypeservice/), a PostgreSQL status doc for Matrix Synapse (pod was never reachable, schema never exported), plus RabbitMQ and Redis operational notes — each store has its own README.

nodes.name: Incident DB-C03 Remediation & Secret Management
nodes.summary: docs/incident-2026-02/db-c03-remediation.md records the remediation of the February 2026 credential exposure: plaintext system-user passwords were removed from scripts/system-users-job.yaml, matrixRegistrationSecret moved from ConfigMap into the system-users-credentials Kubernetes Secret, and SQL quote-escaping added. docs/secret-management.md defines the Secret contract (SealedSecret/SOPS/ESO) and rotation follow-ups.

nodes.name: In-Cluster MariaDB Client
nodes.summary: k8s/mariadb-client provides a kustomize-deployed database client (deployment, service, ingress, configmap) for admin access to MariaDB inside the cluster. Legacy operational tooling — with the repo archived, current in-cluster tooling is owned by ORISO-Helm.

nodes.name: New Environment Initialization (legacy)
nodes.summary: Historical bootstrap path: scripts/database-initialize.yaml provisions the databases → per-service schema.sql files create the tables → scripts/system-users-job.yaml creates system users (reading credentials from the system-users-credentials Secret and writing Matrix credentials into userservice); MongoDB collections restored from the tracked BSON dumps. Superseded by ORISO-Helm charts plus per-service Liquibase for current environments.

nodes.name: SQL Escaping Test
nodes.summary: tests/test-sql-escaping.sh validates the single-quote escaping used when interpolating secret values into the system-users MariaDB heredoc — added as part of the DB-C03 remediation.

nodes.name: ORISO-Keycloak
nodes.summary: Repository ORISO-Keycloak — 356 nodes, 348 edges, built from 367e488d, 16 domain concepts/flows.

nodes.name: Realm Management (online-beratung)
nodes.summary: realm.json carries the 'online-beratung' realm definition — clients, roles, and auth settings. Since July it is Helm-templated ({{ .Values.global.keycloakAuthServerUrl }} / adminDomainName placeholders in redirect URIs and web origins), binds directGrantFlow to the custom 'direct-grant-2fa' flow, sets emailTheme 'oriso', and adds a confidential 'user-service' client with service accounts enabled. Realm roles include restricted-agency-admin (added June 2026); there is NO global-support role in this repo's export at the pinned commit.

nodes.name: Custom ORISO Keycloak Image (26.6.3-otp)
nodes.summary: This repo owns the custom Keycloak image: stock quay.io/keycloak/keycloak:26.6.3 plus the vendored otp-config SPI jar and the 'oriso' email theme, published by CI as ghcr.io/openresilienceinitiative/oriso-keycloak:26.6.3-otp (plus dev/pre-dev branch tags and release/keycloak-* release tags). The ORISO Helm chart references the published image only; SPI source, theme, and build workflow live here.

nodes.name: OTP Config SPI (vendored, ADR-013)
nodes.summary: Vendored fork of Onlineberatung/onlineberatung-keycloak-otp (AGPL, commit fbafb2b), ported to Keycloak 26.6.3. Exposes /realms/<realm>/otp-config/** REST endpoints that the UserService calls for 2FA setup (fetch-otp-setup-info, setup-otp, delete-otp, send-verification-mail, setup-otp-mail); callers must present a bearer token holding the realm role 'technical'. Also registers the direct-grant authenticators app-authenticator (TOTP challenge JSON) and email-authenticator (login-time email OTP).

nodes.name: Email OTP Credentials (MAIL_OTP)
nodes.summary: MAIL_OTP credential type with its own CredentialProvider/Factory. The July 2026 'code not matching' fix registered the MailOtpCredentialProviderFactory as an SPI (it previously was not, so the verify hop found no credential and returned 400), purges pending-but-unverified credentials on resend, deletes all mail OTP credentials on teardown, and sends the verification mail through a UserModelDelegate so the account email is not persisted before the OTP is verified.

nodes.name: direct-grant-2fa Authentication Flow
nodes.summary: Custom top-level direct-grant flow: validate-username → validate-password → conditional sub-flows app-otp-conditional (conditional-user-configured, app-authenticator, direct-grant-validate-otp) and email-otp-conditional (conditional-user-configured, email-authenticator with email-otp-config). Bound as the realm's Direct Grant Flow in realm.json for fresh imports; scripts/keycloak-apply-2fa-flow.sh applies it idempotently to existing realms via kcadm, preserving the existing email-otp-config id from the execution row.

nodes.name: ORISO Email Theme (generated from design system)
nodes.summary: The 'oriso' Keycloak email theme (otp-email and password-reset templates, de/en message bundles, orisoPlatformName/color/URL theme properties) is GENERATED from the ORISO-Frontend email design system ('npm run emails:keycloak') and copied in via scripts/sync-email-theme.sh — do not edit by hand. Theme lookups carry their own defaults so an operator can override any property per realm. The same theme also lives in ORISO-Helm; both copies must be synced or one silently wins at deploy time.

nodes.name: Legacy Kubernetes Manifests (caritas namespace)
nodes.summary: keycloak-deployment.yaml / keycloak-service.yaml / ingress.yaml are the LEGACY raw manifests (still pin quay.io/keycloak/keycloak:20.0.5 in start-dev mode with inline admin credentials). Current deployments come from the ORISO-Helm chart referencing the custom 26.6.3-otp image; these manifests and DEPLOYMENT.md/STATUS.md describe the old single-node setup and have not been updated.

nodes.name: HTTP Access Mode (SSL requirement disabled)
nodes.summary: Keycloak requires HTTPS by default; in ORISO, nginx terminates TLS and internal services talk HTTP. configure-http-access.sh must run after every deployment to disable the SSL requirement for all realms, otherwise authentication fails with 'HTTPS required'. realm.json itself still declares sslRequired=external; the script flips the live realm.

nodes.name: Realm Backup
nodes.summary: backup/realm-backup.sh exports the 'online-beratung' realm from the running Keycloak pod (kubectl exec) into timestamped backups in the repo's backup directory.

nodes.name: 2FA Setup via otp-config REST
nodes.summary: UserService (technical-role bearer token) calls /realms/online-beratung/otp-config/**: fetch-otp-setup-info returns secret/QR data, setup-otp activates app TOTP, send-verification-mail generates a MAIL_OTP credential and emails the code, setup-otp-mail verifies it and activates email OTP, delete-otp tears everything down (all mail OTP credentials, not just the default).

nodes.name: Email OTP Login (direct grant)
nodes.summary: Password grant hits the direct-grant-2fa flow → email-otp-conditional → email-authenticator: without an otp param it generates a code (MemoryOtpService), sends it via the realm's SMTP settings using the oriso otp-email template, and returns the otpType challenge JSON; with an otp param it validates and completes the grant. App TOTP takes the parallel app-otp-conditional branch via app-authenticator and the stock validate-otp.

nodes.name: Image Build & Publish
nodes.summary: CI (feature/PR/main workflows plus a release/keycloak-* release workflow) builds the otp-config SPI with Maven, assembles the Dockerfile (SPI jar into /opt/keycloak/providers, themes into /opt/keycloak/themes, kc.sh build), and pushes ghcr.io/openresilienceinitiative/oriso-keycloak tags (26.6.3-otp, dev, pre-dev, release tags). Helm consumes the published image only.

nodes.name: Email Theme Sync from Design System
nodes.summary: Change email copy/design in ORISO-Frontend src/emails → 'npm run emails:keycloak' generates the Keycloak flavour (message-bundle copy, Keycloak model variables; see ADR-020) → scripts/sync-email-theme.sh copies dist/keycloak/email into keycloak-image/themes/oriso/email → rebuild image; the twin copy in ORISO-Helm must be synced with its own script.

nodes.name: Apply 2FA Flow to Existing Realm
nodes.summary: For realms that predate the 2FA flow: kubectl exec into the Keycloak pod (must run the oriso image) → keycloak-apply-2fa-flow.sh logs kcadm in, rebinds directGrantFlow to stock 'direct grant', captures the existing email-otp-config id from the execution row (flat JSON, parser-safe), deletes and recreates direct-grant-2fa with both conditional sub-flows, restores the config, and rebinds the realm.

nodes.name: Deploy & Configure (legacy path)
nodes.summary: Legacy raw-manifest path: apply deployment/service/ingress → wait for the pod → run configure-http-access.sh to disable the SSL requirement. Current deployments instead go through the ORISO-Helm keycloak chart with the custom image; the HTTP-access step remains relevant wherever nginx terminates TLS.

nodes.name: Backup & Restore Realm
nodes.summary: realm-backup.sh exports the realm from the running pod to a timestamped file; realm.json is the canonical import used to restore or re-provision the realm (now containing Helm placeholders, so it must be rendered/substituted before a raw import).

nodes.name: ORISO-Kubernetes
nodes.summary: Repository ORISO-Kubernetes — 147 nodes, 13 edges, built from 10232408, 3 domain concepts/flows.

nodes.name: LEGACY: Archived, superseded by ORISO-Helm
nodes.summary: This repository is ARCHIVED upstream (Neusta-owned, read-only) with no commits since 2026-07-09. The canonical, actively maintained deployment repository is ORISO-Helm. Treat everything here as historical reference for analysis only — never deploy from or modify this repo.

nodes.name: Platform Deployment Configuration (historical)
nodes.summary: Historical Kubernetes deployment configuration for the whole ORISO platform: infrastructure (MariaDB, MongoDB, RabbitMQ, Redis), Keycloak, backend services (Tenant, User, Agency, ConsultingType, Upload), frontend & admin, communication (Matrix Synapse, Element, LiveKit), and monitoring (SigNoz, Health Dashboard). Superseded by ORISO-Helm; last change wired the LiveKit token service websocket URL.

nodes.name: ConfigMaps, Helm & Ingress
nodes.summary: The repo groups its manifests into configmaps/ (captured live service configuration snapshots), helm/ (umbrella chart oriso-platform plus per-service charts) and ingress/ (numbered host/TLS routing manifests applied via apply-ingress.sh), with docs/ holding the multitenancy specification.

nodes.name: ORISO-Helm
nodes.summary: Repository ORISO-Helm — 480 nodes, 298 edges, built from c45eaaab, 23 domain concepts/flows.

nodes.name: Full-Stack Platform Chart
nodes.summary: Umbrella Helm chart (name online-counseling, version 2.0.2) deploying the entire ORISO platform: Keycloak, MariaDB, MongoDB, RabbitMQ, Redis, Matrix/Synapse, LiveKit + MatrixRTC auth, Element Call, the nginx ingress controller, an optional SigNoz observability stack, the health dashboard, and all ORISO backend/frontend services. Infra subcharts are vendored unpacked under charts/ with file:// dependencies; service workloads are rendered directly from templates/<service>/.

nodes.name: Config/Secret Split (values.yaml + secrets.yaml)
nodes.summary: Configuration is split across two gitignored files created from tracked *.default templates: values.yaml (domain, realm, Matrix server name, image references) and secrets.yaml (all credentials). Several secrets are fail-closed at render time: agencyService.serviceEncryptionAppkey and userService.statisticsMessageCountHmacSecret make the chart refuse to render when blank, and password-reset/account-invite base URLs fail closed at runtime when unset.

nodes.name: Environment Overlays (prod-safe baseline + values-dev/values-prod)
nodes.summary: values.yaml.default is a prod-safe baseline (springProfilesActive prod, no dummy-data seeding, OTP allowed by default, encryption never toggleable). Per-environment behaviour is layered via untracked values-dev.yaml / values-prod.yaml overlays instead of separate copies; production is deployed by the hoster via ArgoCD. Overlays only change test friction and wiring — there is deliberately no dev encryption-off mode.

nodes.name: Keycloak Subchart, Custom Theme, and User Bootstrap
nodes.summary: charts/keycloak carries the realm definition (realm.json, imported on first start only), deployment templates, and the ORISO custom theme (login pages, OTP email templates, DE/EN messages, Nunito fonts) mounted via theme configmaps. The image is the ORISO-built oriso-keycloak (OTP support). A parent-chart Job bootstraps Keycloak users, and realm import on pod restart is guarded so it never re-imports destructively.

nodes.name: MariaDB Subchart: Canonical SQL Schema Mirrors
nodes.summary: Since 2026-06-30 charts/mariadb/sql-schemas/ is the canonical home of the per-service MariaDB schema mirrors (agencyservice, consultingtypeservice, tenantservice, uploadservice, userservice) — ORISO-Database is archived. Environments that force SPRING_LIQUIBASE_ENABLED=false (Pre-Dev configmap) rely on these mirrors plus manual ALTER runbooks; legacy Liquibase changelog overrides are normalized for compatibility.

nodes.name: Matrix-Only Messaging Stack (ADR-005, no legacy chat)
nodes.summary: Synapse homeserver with dedicated Postgres statefulset (including WAL-archive/PITR backup and restore scripting in its config). ADR-005 invariants are enforced: the homeserver is non-federated (empty federation_domain_whitelist), server_name must never be a bare IP (static guardrail with self-test), and a render guard bans any Rocket.Chat or embedded-Jitsi remnant from ever returning to the chart.

nodes.name: LiveKit SFU + MatrixRTC Authorization
nodes.summary: Calls run on a LiveKit SFU (hostNetwork) fronted by two MatrixRTC authorization deployments: the upstream authorization service and the ORISO policy gateway. Grants are fail-closed: every new call/reconnect is resolved against UserService using the dedicated callPolicyToken; UserService unavailability never yields a permissive grant. A bootstrap Job registers a non-admin Matrix membership-reader user and patches its access token into matrixrtc-auth-secrets. Single-node rollouts use strategy Recreate with validation errors for unsafe topologies; NetworkPolicies restrict ingress-controller and homeserver reachability.

nodes.name: Element Call Widget Deployment
nodes.summary: Element Call (ORISO-built ghcr image) is deployed as the call widget UI with its own configmap/deployment/service plus dedicated ingresses: an element-call host ingress, a main-host static-asset ingress, and a /room compatibility ingress on the main domain.

nodes.name: Single-Domain Ingress Routing
nodes.summary: The chart ships its own ingress-nginx controller and ~25 Ingress objects routing everything under one public domain: /service/* paths to backend services (main-ingress), tenant public/tenantadmin/access/id rewrites, unauthenticated GET /media/{id} to TenantService for legal-text images (epic Admin#366 WP-3a), Matrix client-server API, LiveKit SFU/JWT endpoints, Element Call, ACME, and /signoz. TenantService single-domain access flags are render-tested.

nodes.name: Digest-Pinned Cutover Release Process
nodes.summary: For the coordinated Matrix-only/Matryoshka cutover, Frontend, Element Call, UserService, AgencyService, Synapse and both MatrixRTC images accept only complete repository@sha256 digests. scripts/cutover-release-preflight.py validates a cross-repo release manifest fail-closed (STOP_SHIP placeholders, zero/wrong digests, missing PR or security evidence, forbidden legacy render artifacts) and emits the exact Helm digest overlay used between environment values and secrets.

nodes.name: Install-Time Bootstrap Jobs
nodes.summary: Helm hooks seed the platform after the schema layer is ready: a tenant bootstrap Job (tenant-bootstrap.sql), a topic bootstrap Job for ConsultingTypeService, a Keycloak user bootstrap Job, and a MongoDB user-creation Job. Hooks are install-only (never re-run destructively on upgrade), configmaps are namespaced, and AUTO_INCREMENT sequences are advanced with valid setval-style calls so seeded rows never collide with runtime inserts.

nodes.name: Demo Baseline and Pre-Demo Gate
nodes.summary: Helm-owned demo/initial-delivery baseline for customer-facing demo environments: sync and check SQL scripts plus a manifest, wrapped by a one-command gate script (demo-baseline-gate.sh all) that verifies demo readiness against a deployed environment before a customer demo.

nodes.name: SOPS+age Test-Credential Store and Keycloak Seeding
nodes.summary: Central, encrypted-in-git store of dev/pre-dev test-user credentials (SOPS + age) readable by humans and agents. seed-keycloak-users.sh creates users via the Keycloak Admin API — no CONFIGURE_TOTP required action, so seeded users bypass interactive 2FA — supports Keycloak user attributes, and writes created credentials back into the store. Production credentials are explicitly excluded.

nodes.name: Optional SigNoz Observability Stack
nodes.summary: SigNoz (with vendored ClickHouse/Zookeeper/Postgres/Redpanda subcharts) is an optional dependency gated by signoz.enabled. Enabling it auto-points backend services at the in-cluster OTLP HTTP collector via helper templates; the UI is served at /signoz on the main domain (bare /signoz redirects to /signoz/). Prod telemetry stays off by default and a KDG-safe pseudonymization flag (telemetryPseudonymizationEnabled) is built but also off pending sign-off.

nodes.name: Render Guard Test Suite
nodes.summary: A Python/bash test layer under tests/ renders the chart (or minimal sub-charts) with helm template and asserts security and operational invariants: statistics HMAC secret required, password-reset/account-invite URLs wired, OTP admin client present, storage classes preserved on upgrade, value-driven image pull policy, Redis-backed availability + Matrix room encryption gates, MatrixRTC call-cutover security, and no legacy chat. guardrail_selftest.sh proves the ADR-005 scanner can actually fail.

nodes.name: Global Support Access (ADR-018) Gate
nodes.summary: Support access (a Global Support Admin helping one consultant in a fresh encrypted 1:1 Matrix room after a live handshake, auto-withdrawn after at most four hours) ships disabled in every environment (userService.supportAccess.enabled=false). The flag gates only new handshakes; enabling it requires a Keycloak realm-role script and migration checks documented in the runbook.

nodes.name: Chart Release Workflow
nodes.summary: Manual workflow_dispatch GitHub Actions workflow (run from main) that tags the release, packages the umbrella chart, and publishes it as an OCI artifact to ghcr.io/openresilienceinitiative/charts. Environment overlay values are excluded from the platform release package.

nodes.name: Deploy Platform
nodes.summary: Copy values.yaml.default and secrets.yaml.default to local gitignored files and fill in domain/realm/credentials → helm upgrade --install with -f values.yaml -f values-<env>.yaml [-f digest-overlay] -f secrets.yaml --wait-for-jobs → subcharts provision Keycloak (realm + theme), MariaDB (schema mirrors), MongoDB, RabbitMQ, Redis, Matrix, LiveKit/MatrixRTC, Element Call, ingress → install-only bootstrap jobs seed tenants, topics, Keycloak and Mongo users.

nodes.name: MatrixRTC Token Bootstrap
nodes.summary: helm install renders matrixrtc-auth-secrets and livekit-config from ignored secrets → the matrixrtc-bootstrap-token Job waits for Synapse, registers or reuses the non-admin membership-reader user, logs in, and patches the real Matrix access token into matrixrtc-auth-secrets → MatrixRTC auth waits for the token, then LiveKit, MatrixRTC auth, and Element Call start without a second bootstrap step → at call time the policy gateway resolves every new call/reconnect against UserService (callPolicyToken, fail-closed) before a LiveKit grant is issued.

nodes.name: Cutover Release (digest-pinned)
nodes.summary: Cross-repo release manifest reaches ready-for-predev with reviewed digests, security evidence and rotated secrets → scripts/cutover-release-preflight.py validates it fail-closed and writes the digest overlay values file → helm upgrade --install with the overlay between environment values and secrets → render guards and the runbook's post-deploy checks confirm no legacy artifacts and no leaked credentials.

nodes.name: Demo Baseline Gate
nodes.summary: Before a customer demo: DEMO_BASE_URL=<env> ./scripts/demo-baseline-gate.sh all → syncs the Helm-owned baseline into MariaDB (demo-baseline-sync.sql), checks invariants (demo-baseline-check.sql, manifest.json), and probes the deployed APIs → pass/fail demo readiness.

nodes.name: Seed Test Users
nodes.summary: scripts/seed-keycloak-users.sh decrypts the SOPS+age test-user store → creates users through the Keycloak Admin API (no CONFIGURE_TOTP required action, optional user attributes) → writes generated credentials back into the encrypted store so humans and agents share one source of test logins.

nodes.name: Release Chart
nodes.summary: Maintainer triggers the release workflow from main with a version input → workflow creates and pushes the Git tag, packages the umbrella chart, and publishes it as an OCI chart to ghcr.io/openresilienceinitiative/charts.
